{"search_note":"I found no reliable 2024 evidence that Kishida:
- ordered prosecutors, courts, or auditors to stand down,
- punished journalists or whistleblowers,
- used security or administrative powers to conceal his own misconduct,
- or ordered retaliation against investigators.

The evidence is therefore absence-of-proof plus positive counterevidence: he cooperated with scrutiny, while the remaining weaknesses are structural and party-system-related rather than a demonstrated abuse of state power by Kishida personally.","evidence":[{"title":"Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"January 4, 2024","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/04kaiken2.html","summary":"Kishida said the LDP would cooperate with prosecutors, created a Political Reform Headquarters, and invited external experts to design transparency rules for political funds. This is direct evidence against using state power to conceal scandal or block scrutiny.","question_ids":["7B.7","7B.6","7B.4"]},{"title":"Embattled Japan PM faces ethics committee, with popularity and budget on the line","publisher":"Reuters","date":"February 28, 2024","url":"https://www.investing.com/news/economy/embattled-japan-pm-faces-ethics-committee-to-save-popularity-and-budget-3319362","summary":"Kishida became the first sitting Japanese prime minister to appear before a parliamentary ethics committee over the funding scandal, and he apologized. This is evidence of tolerating legislative scrutiny rather than neutralizing it.","question_ids":["7B.7","7B.6","7B.4"]},{"title":"Japan prosecutors make first arrest in political funding scandal","publisher":"Reuters","date":"January 7, 2024","url":"https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Japan-prosecutors-make-first-arrest-in-political-funding-scandal-45687976/","summary":"Prosecutors arrested a ruling-party lawmaker over alleged fundraising kickbacks and off-book money. This is negative context for Kishida’s environment, but it also shows prosecutors were able to act, not blocked by the PM.","question_ids":["7B.7","7B.6","7B.4"]},{"title":"Prosecutors indict several LDP faction members over funds scandal","publisher":"Kyodo News","date":"January 19, 2024","url":"https://english.kyodonews.net/news/2024/01/f4d6ea5b7d8f-update1-prosecutors-indict-several-ldp-faction-members-over-funds-scandal.html","summary":"Prosecutors indicted multiple ruling-party faction figures, including a former accountant from Kishida’s group, over undisclosed revenue. This indicates independent investigation reached Kishida’s orbit, not that it was shut down.","question_ids":["7B.7","7B.6","7B.4","7B.5"]},{"title":"Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"June 21, 2024","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202406/21kaiken.html","summary":"Kishida said disclosure thresholds were lowered and that a third-party inspections-and-audits body should be created. That is affirmative evidence that he supported independent oversight rather than hiding political finance from review.","question_ids":["7B.7","7B.6","7B.4"]},{"title":"Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"August 14, 2024","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202408/14kaiken.html","summary":"Kishida said the LDP presidential race should be transparent, with free and vigorous debate, and that he would step aside and support the winner chosen by vote. This is evidence against trying to use office to entrench himself or suppress accountability.","question_ids":["7B.7","7B.6","7B.5","7B.3"]},{"title":"Japan: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2024","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/japan/freedom-world/2024","summary":"Freedom House says Japan generally operates with openness and transparency, though some officials withhold information in scandal contexts and press-club structures constrain access. This is mixed structural context, not evidence that Kishida personally weaponized the state against investigators.","question_ids":["7B.7","7B.6"]},{"title":"Japan: Freedom on the Net 2024 Country Report","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2024","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/japan/freedom-net/2024","summary":"Freedom House says government pressure and the kisha kurabu system contribute to self-censorship and restricted access for some journalists and outlets. This is negative background on media independence, but it is structural and not Kishida-specific repression.","question_ids":["7B.7","7B.6"]},{"title":"World Report 2024: Japan","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024","url":"https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/japan","summary":"HRW says Japan’s “hostage justice” system still involved coercive questioning, repeated arrests, denial of bail, and weak legal access. This undercuts any claim that Kishida fully fixed oversight institutions, but it does not show him using them to crush investigators or whistleblowers.","question_ids":["7B.7","7B.6"]}]}
